name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q01 - Ciliated epithelium, glands, cell junctions and compound epithelium

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding epithelial tissues:

Statement I: Ciliated epithelium consists of columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia on their free surface and is present in the inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

Statement II: Endocrine glands lack ducts and secrete their products called hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

Statement III: Adhering junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue, whereas tight junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together.

Statement IV: Compound epithelium covers the dry surface of the skin and the moist surface of the buccal cavity and pharynx.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Epithelial tissues exhibit structural specialisations for directional transport (cilia), secretion (exocrine and endocrine glands), intercellular linkage (junctions), and multi-layered protection (compound epithelium).

Step 2: Evaluation of Ciliated Epithelium and Endocrine Glands
Columnar or cuboidal cells bearing cilia on their free surface form ciliated epithelium, which moves particles or mucus in a specific direction in hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes. Additionally, endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland. Hence, both of these claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cell Junctions
Tight junctions help stop substances from leaking across a tissue, whereas adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Reversing these two roles makes the claim about cell junctions incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Compound Epithelium
Compound epithelium is multi-layered to protect against chemical and mechanical stresses, covering the dry surface of the skin as well as the moist surfaces of the buccal cavity, pharynx, and inner lining of salivary and pancreatic ducts. Hence, this claim is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding ciliated epithelium, endocrine glands, and compound epithelium are correct, while the claim swapping the functions of tight and adhering junctions is incorrect.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q02 - Dense irregular tissue, cartilage, bone marrow and muscle striations

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding connective and muscular tissues:

Statement I: Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) oriented differently and is present in the skin.

Statement II: In adults, cartilage is present in the tip of the nose, outer ear joints, and between adjacent bones of the vertebral column.

Statement III: The bone marrow in some bones serves as the site of production of blood cells.

Statement IV: Smooth muscle fibres are cylindrical, bundled in parallel arrays, and show prominent striations.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Connective tissues vary in fibre orientation and matrix rigidity (dense irregular, cartilage, bone), while muscle tissues differ in cell shape and the presence or absence of striations.

Step 2: Evaluation of Dense Irregular Tissue and Cartilage
Dense irregular connective tissue contains fibroblasts and differently oriented collagen fibres and occurs in the skin. Cartilage persists in adults at the tip of the nose, outer ear joints, between adjacent vertebrae, and in limbs and hands. Thus, both of these claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Bone Marrow
Bones provide structural support and protection, and the bone marrow inside some bones is the site where blood cells are produced. Thus, this claim is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Smooth Muscle Structure
Smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform) and do not show striations, unlike skeletal muscle fibres which are striated and bundled in parallel. Thus, claiming that smooth muscle fibres show prominent striations is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first three claims regarding dense irregular connective tissue, adult cartilage locations, and bone marrow function are correct, whereas the fourth claim regarding smooth muscle striations is incorrect.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q03 - Earthworm castings, spermathecal apertures, calciferous glands and caecae

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding the earthworm (*Pheretima*):

Statement I: In gardens, earthworms can be traced by their faecal deposits known as worm castings.

Statement II: Four pairs of spermathecal apertures are situated on the ventro-lateral sides of the intersegmental grooves of the 5th–9th segments.

Statement III: Calciferous glands present in the stomach neutralise the humic acid present in humus.

Statement IV: A pair of short and conical intestinal caecae project from the intestine on the 15th segment.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms exhibit characteristic external markings, segmentally arranged reproductive apertures, and specialised digestive structures adapted to feeding on decaying organic matter mixed with soil.

Step 2: Evaluation of Worm Castings and Spermathecal Apertures
Earthworms inhabit burrows in moist soil and leave faecal deposits called worm castings. Four pairs of spermathecal apertures are located ventro-laterally in the intersegmental grooves of the 5th–9th segments. Both of these claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Calciferous Glands
The stomach extends from segments 9–14 and contains calciferous glands that neutralise the humic acid present in humus ingested with soil. This claim is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Intestinal Caecae
Although the intestine begins from the 15th segment onwards, the pair of short and conical intestinal caecae projects from the intestine specifically on the 26th segment, not the 15th segment. Hence, this claim is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding worm castings, spermathecal apertures, and calciferous glands are correct, while the claim placing intestinal caecae on the 15th segment is incorrect.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q04 - Earthworm pharyngeal nephridia, sense organs, spermathecae and accessory glands

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements about the anatomy of the earthworm:

Statement I: Pharyngeal nephridia are present as three paired tufts in the 4th, 5th, and 6th segments.

Statement II: The sensory system lacks eyes but possesses light- and touch-sensitive receptor cells as well as specialised chemoreceptors on the anterior part of the worm.

Statement III: Four pairs of spermathecae are located in the 6th–9th segments (one pair in each segment) to receive and store spermatozoa during copulation.

Statement IV: Two pairs of accessory glands are present in the reproductive system, one pair each in the 17th and 19th segments.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Earthworms display precise segmental localisation of their excretory nephridia, anterior sensory receptors, and reproductive organs.

Step 2: Evaluation of Pharyngeal Nephridia and Sense Organs
Pharyngeal nephridia occur as three paired tufts in the 4th, 5th, and 6th segments. Earthworms do not have eyes, yet they possess light- and touch-sensitive receptor cells to detect light intensity and ground vibrations, along with chemoreceptors (taste receptors) on the anterior end. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Spermathecae and Accessory Glands
Four pairs of spermathecae reside in the 6th–9th segments (one pair per segment) to receive and store spermatozoa during copulation. Furthermore, two pairs of accessory glands are located one pair each in the 17th and 19th segments. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four propositions accurately describe the segmental positions and functions of pharyngeal nephridia, sensory receptors, spermathecae, and accessory glands in the earthworm.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q05 - Cockroach head, crop, haemolymph and heart structure

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding *Periplaneta americana*:

Statement I: The triangular head lies anteriorly at right angles to the longitudinal body axis and is formed by the fusion of six segments.

Statement II: The oesophagus opens into a sac-like structure called the crop, which is used for storing food.

Statement III: The haemolymph is composed of colourless plasma and haemocytes, bathing the visceral organs in the haemocoel.

Statement IV: The heart is a single-chambered organ lying along the mid-ventral line of the abdomen.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cockroaches possess a fused head capsule, a foregut specialised for food storage and grinding, and an open blood vascular system with a dorsal tubular heart.

Step 2: Evaluation of Head and Crop
The triangular head lies at right angles to the longitudinal body axis, is formed by the fusion of six segments, and moves freely via a flexible neck. In the foregut, the oesophagus opens into a sac-like crop used for storing food. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Haemolymph and Heart
In the open circulatory system, visceral organs in the haemocoel are bathed in haemolymph consisting of colourless plasma and haemocytes. However, the heart is an elongated muscular tube lying along the mid-dorsal line of the thorax and abdomen, differentiated into funnel-shaped chambers with ostia—not a single-chambered mid-ventral organ. Thus, the claim about haemolymph is correct, while the claim about the heart is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first three claims regarding the head, crop, and haemolymph are correct, whereas the fourth claim describing the heart as single-chambered and mid-ventral is incorrect.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q06 - Cockroach brood pouch, ganglia, decapitation survival and oothecae

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding the cockroach:

Statement I: In females, the 7th sternum is boat-shaped and together with the 8th and 9th sterna forms a brood or genital pouch.

Statement II: The ventral nervous system includes three ganglia in the thorax and six ganglia in the abdomen.

Statement III: If the head of a cockroach is cut off, it dies immediately because the entire nervous system is confined to the head.

Statement IV: On an average, a female produces 9–10 oothecae, each containing 14–16 fertilised eggs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cockroaches exhibit distinct abdominal sternal modifications in females, a decentralised ventral nerve cord, and encapsulation of fertilised eggs in oothecae.

Step 2: Evaluation of Female Brood Pouch and Ganglia
In female cockroaches, the boat-shaped 7th sternum together with the 8th and 9th sterna forms the brood (genital) pouch containing the female gonopore, spermathecal pores, and collateral glands. The nervous system has three thoracic ganglia and six abdominal ganglia joined by paired ventral longitudinal connectives. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Decapitation Survival
The head holds only a small part of the nervous system (the supra-oesophageal ganglion), while most of the nervous system is distributed along the ventral side of the body. Consequently, a cockroach can still live for as long as one week if its head is cut off. Thus, claiming it dies immediately because the entire nervous system is in the head is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Oothecae Production
Fertilised eggs are encased in dark reddish to blackish-brown oothecae (about 8 mm long); females produce an average of 9–10 oothecae, each containing 14–16 eggs. This claim is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the female brood pouch, thoracic/abdominal ganglia, and oothecae are correct, whereas the claim regarding immediate death upon decapitation is incorrect.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q07 - Frog mimicry, limb digits, duodenal ducts and water absorption

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding *Rana tigrina*:

Statement I: Frogs can change colour to hide from enemies (camouflage), a protective coloration called mimicry.

Statement II: The hindlimbs end in five digits and are larger and more muscular than the forelimbs, which end in four digits.

Statement III: The duodenum receives bile from the gall bladder and pancreatic juices from the pancreas through a common bile duct.

Statement IV: Frogs drink large quantities of freshwater through the mouth to maintain their moist skin.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Indian bullfrogs (*Rana tigrina*) display adaptive coloration, specialised limb anatomy for swimming and leaping, vertebrate digestive secretions into the duodenum, and cutaneous water uptake.

Step 2: Evaluation of Mimicry and Limb Digits
Frogs alter their skin colour between grasses and dry land for camouflage, which is termed mimicry. Their larger, muscular hindlimbs end in five webbed digits, whereas their forelimbs end in four digits. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Duodenal Secretions
Partially digested chyme passes from the stomach into the duodenum, which receives bile (to emulsify fats) from the gall bladder and pancreatic juice (to digest carbohydrates and proteins) from the pancreas via a common bile duct. This claim is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Water Intake
A frog never drinks water through its mouth; instead, it absorbs water directly through its smooth, moist skin. Thus, claiming that frogs drink large quantities of water is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first three claims regarding protective coloration, limb digit counts, and the common bile duct are correct, while the claim that frogs drink water through the mouth is incorrect.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_Q08 - Frog portal systems, ureotelism, cranial nerves and development

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements about the physiology and development of frogs:

Statement I: Frogs possess special venous connections between the liver and intestine (hepatic portal system) as well as between the kidney and lower parts of the body (renal portal system).

Statement II: Frogs excrete urea as their primary nitrogenous waste and are therefore ureotelic animals.

Statement III: Ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain, and the medulla oblongata passes out through the foramen magnum to continue as the spinal cord.

Statement IV: Fertilisation is external and takes place in water, and development involves a larval stage called a tadpole that undergoes metamorphosis.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
As amphibians, frogs possess dual portal venous systems, ureotelic nitrogenous excretion, a cranium-enclosed brain with ten pairs of cranial nerves, and aquatic external fertilisation with metamorphosis.

Step 2: Evaluation of Portal Systems and Excretion
Frogs have both a hepatic portal system (connecting intestine and liver) and a renal portal system (connecting lower body parts and kidneys). Their kidneys separate and excrete urea, making them ureotelic. Both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Nervous System and Reproduction
Ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from the frog's brain, and the medulla oblongata exits through the foramen magnum into the vertebral column as the spinal cord. A mature female lays 2500–3000 ova at a time, fertilisation is external in water, and the resulting tadpole larva undergoes metamorphosis into an adult frog. Both claims are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four propositions accurately represent the circulatory, excretory, neural, and reproductive characteristics of the frog.

answer.text: All Statements I, II, III and IV
